reason: Central claim and all headline results are for a policy whose weights are updated by GRPO (veRL); evaluation is run without experience guidance. Synthetic tasks, the experience pool and the LLM judge are training-time aids produced by stronger external LLMs. The only retained non-weight effect (experience injection at inference, Table 4 '+ exp.') is a minor dev-set side result, not the claim. Per frozen rubric A3 (evaluated object = weights) this is out of scope; boundary case flagged for the aggregator. Not scored.

paper.title: AgentEvolver: Towards Efficient Self-Evolving Agent System
paper.central_claim: AgentEvolver, an RL-based self-evolving agent training system with three mechanisms (self-questioning: LLM-synthesised tasks; self-navigating: experience pool, experience-mixed rollouts and experience stripping/selective boosting; self-attributing: LLM step-wise credit assignment) improves Qwen2.5-7B/14B on AppWorld and BFCL-v3 with higher exploration efficiency and sample utilisation than vanilla GRPO.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured model type only

sections_read: 7.5-7.6 attribution / context-template results (skimmed, not needed for scope ruling)

evidence.quote: , a self-evolving agent system that leverages the semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to drive autonomous agent learning.
evidence.support_explanation: The system is framed as agent learning (policy training), driven by LLM-based task/reward/experience components.

evidence.quote: Finally, Sample Construction & Model Optimization applies self-attributing to convert trajectories and intermediate states into training samples with fine-grained credit assignment (e.g., step-level attribution) and updates the policy parameters accordingly.
evidence.support_explanation: The improver terminates in a parameter update of the policy; the reported products are trained weights.

evidence.quote: we report only the results without experience guidance to provide a fair assessment of the impact of experience incorporation.
evidence.support_explanation: Reported gains are for the trained policy evaluated without the retained experience pool; the pool is not part of the evaluated artifact.

evidence.quote: prior to policy gradient computation, retrieved experience tokens are removed from the training samples.
evidence.support_explanation: By design the experience is stripped so that learning is internalised in weights rather than carried by the retained store.
The only non-weight retained effect: inference-time experience injection raises zero-shot avg@4 from 25.2 to 30.9 on the dev set; the RL baseline (57.2) dwarfs it and the headline path is weights.
Headline table compares zero-shot vs progressively trained policies; there is no vanilla-GRPO-on-original-tasks row in Table 1.

evidence.quote: We create environment profiles for the Appworld and BFCL benchmarks, as well as user preferences.
evidence.support_explanation: Environment profiles and user preferences are hand-authored inputs to task synthesis.

evidence.quote: even without training, contextualized guidance allows the model to explore more effectively and produce superior outcomes.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's reading of the zero-shot experience-injection result, the single in-scope-flavoured side finding.

evidence.quote: We aim to unify exploration, experience abstraction, self-attribution, and inference within a single model
evidence.support_explanation: Current system relies on separate stronger LLMs (Qwen-Plus, Qwen3-235B judge, Qwen-Max) for tasks, judging and attribution; single-model self-evolution is stated as future work.

signatures.object: Policy weights of Qwen2.5-7B/14B, trained by GRPO on LLM-synthesised tasks with LLM-judged and LLM-attributed rewards and an experience-mixed rollout strategy; auxiliary non-weight artifacts: synthetic task set, experience pool, judge prompts
signatures.information: Environment profiles and user preferences (human-written); exploration by Qwen-Plus; reference solutions from exploration trajectories; experience pool built from policy rollouts; judge LLMs (Qwen3-235B, Qwen-Max)
signatures.operation: Explore -> synthesise and filter tasks -> rollouts (half experience-guided) -> LLM judge reward and step-wise GOOD/BAD attribution -> GRPO update with experience tokens stripped and selective boosting
signatures.selection_rule_data: Lexical/semantic dedup, reference-solution executability check for tasks; experience validation by an LLM evaluator
signatures.persistence: Weights persist; experience pool and task set are training-time assets, not evaluated artifacts
signatures.later_use: Trained policy evaluated without experience on avg@8 / best@8
signatures.failure_boundary: Only two benchmarks, two model sizes, 'preliminary experiments'

claims.text: Combining self-questioning, self-navigating and self-attributing improves policy performance on AppWorld and BFCL-v3 over zero-shot Qwen2.5 and over the cumulative ablations
claims.setting: GRPO with veRL, 8x A100, avg@8 and best@8

unresolved: Boundary question: whether the experience-pool inference result (Table 4) should make this a B-class component paper

scope_analysis: Excluded: weight-updating self-improvement whose reported product is a trained policy (rubric A3). Non-weight components (synthetic task set, experience pool, LLM judge) are produced from execution feedback and retained during training, but they are not evaluated as retained artifacts for later tasks; evaluation is done without experience (E003) and experience is deliberately stripped before the gradient step (E004). Boundary note for the aggregator: Table 4 shows inference-time experience injection (+5.7 avg@4 on the 14B dev set, E005) and the pool is built by the shared ReMe pipeline, so an in-scope B-type reading would be a narrow experience-retrieval component with a dev-set-only effect; that would not change the central claim. If the aggregator rules the boundary in scope, plausible RS candidates are self_supervised_signal_engineering and generative_process_redesign, and plausible domain cards are self_generate_the_curriculum (H23) and abstract_experience_into_guidance (H00); this seat has not scored the paper.
rationale: Evaluated product is a GRPO-trained policy; experience pool and tasks are training aids, eval runs without experience. Out of scope (A3, boundary).
